items.followUp: What are simple tissues? Describe the structure and function of parenchyma and collenchyma.

rubric.why: A compound tissue consists of more than one type of cell working together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a compound tissue is made of different cell types working together.

rubric.why: Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves and other parts of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the transport of water and mineral salts from the roots to the plant.

rubric.why: Xylem consists of vessels, tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres; all its elements are dead at maturity except the parenchyma.
rubric.description: Names the xylem components and describes which are living or dead.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for naming the four xylem components and stating that the elements are dead at maturity except for xylem parenchyma.

rubric.why: Phloem transports prepared food from leaves to other parts of the plant and consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres; all are living except the fibres.
rubric.description: Explains the function and components of phloem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing food transport and naming phloem components, including that phloem fibres are dead while the other components are living.

modelAnswer: Compound tissues are made of more than one type of cell working together to perform a function.
Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves and other parts of the plant.
Xylem consists of vessels, tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.
All xylem elements are dead at maturity except xylem parenchyma.
Phloem transports prepared food from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
Phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres; all are living except the phloem fibres.
